Have you ever been seen naked by somebody or saw somebody naked accidentally? I rented a ratty, hole in the wall apartment for a brief period when I went to University. I say ratty because the very first night I moved in I opened my door later to see a huge rat scampering off behind some junk near the wall. The fat, insolent bugger looked as though he was accustomed to tenants putting out garbage that hour. It was an old building that was sectioned off into a few rooms which in time were further subdivided into smaller rooms. It was like a barracks but ugly, poorly designed and devoid of any taste whatsoever. The entire upstairs and downstairs each shared one tiny kitchen and one bathroom area. I wondered what was the need for a door to the bathroom when there was a gap from the door to the door frame that was so wide you could peep in and see clearly anyone who was having a bath or a shit. As one could imagine it was rented solely by lesser income bracket males. It was a common to see tasteless, junky buildings such as this in any highly populated area in Trinidad. Practically zero laws were enforced in regards to building code so it seemed as though the owners were all competing to build the biggest, ugliest brick and mortar ant-nest in the world. The neighbouring building was no exception but it was a larger, newer and much more spacious apartment complex. The apartment was rented by students who clearly belonged to upper middle class families. The large spacious building was so tall and stately that it seemed to look down on our decrepit little hovel like a deformed, underdeveloped sibling. One night as I lay on my thin mattress, deciding whether to bear with the heat of the poorly ventilated cell-like room or open the window and bear with the plague of mosquitoes waiting patiently to enter I heard a noise that resonated in my ears and in my groin. It was the sound of female laughter. It wasn't just any laughter. It was the lusty, playful laughter of a pair of attractive young women. I looked at the window and saw an open door from the second floor apartment next door and from inside the door the well lit room revealed a girl walking several times past the door completely naked. One could imagine how a lonely, young, hot-blooded male cramped in a tiny room without a single form of entertainment at his disposal would feel to see this tender female figure darting back and forth in front of his eyes without a thread of clothing. It was like seeing flashes of heaven. I quickly turned off my lights so the girl wouldn't catch me peeping and I rooted myself by the window, hungry for more. However nothing else happened and the door closed. The following evening I was home at night trying to read a book on Investments when my ears pricked. The familiar sound of laughter could be heard. Almost on instinct I flew to my light switch and turned it off. I went to the window. This time two girls darted back and forth, nude, in front of the door. I wondered if I was dreaming. At one point, one of them stood by the doorway for several seconds, looking at her phone, allowing one to absorb the view of her body. ‘Somebody’s going to see us,’ one of them said and the mischievous nymphs laughed heartily. They both couldn't be older than 20 and from the way they interacted they were quite possibly related. It was obvious that they both enjoyed exhibition. This was not an accident. I looked at my watch. It was 6:45pm. It was around this time yesterday that one of them gave their show. Immediately the door closed for the night. The show was over. At 6:30 the following evening I was like a perverted sentry posted at my windowsill in the darkness, resolute on catching a third viewing. I wished to God I had had the means to buy binoculars. Why couldn't I been born to a well off family and living in the apartment next to them? I saw them as they came from their classes, heading towards their apartment; a pair of Indian girls, bespectacled and quite innocent looking the way they postured themselves and wore rather baggy, unbecoming clothes. In attire they were completely different creatures, almost nerdy. They looked the dictionary image of graduates from an all girls’ Convent school. They both appeared somber and reticent. They dragged themselves forward without a word to one another and went indoors, closing the door behind them halfway. What was with the moodiness? Did someone report them? Did their family find out about their exhibitions and issued a stern warning? Did someone record them and circulated their nude videos around campus? I hoped to God not. In my steaming little hovel I was hungry for more. I could hear them arguing about something for a few seconds. I could hear them laughing. I could hear them eating. I could hear the dishes being washed and packed away. C’mon! I looked at my watch. It was a minute or so before 7pm. Was tonight going to be a no-show? As the thought came to mind the door opened and the younger girl stepped forward staring at her phone, naked as the Sahara. She stood for a few seconds, myself completely succumbed in lust. The other girl shouted to her to close the door and she made a sad face as if to say, ‘Sorry for the late show but it's over now’ and she closed the door. I took a deep breath and went outside my apartment. I hoped that somehow one of them would see me through their window and feel the urge to have a conversation with me. The only thing interested in me were the mosquitoes so I quickly went back inside. I turned on my lights. Suddenly I noticed that practically every apartment that faced the girls had had their lights off and were turning them on as well. Obviously I wasn't the only one in my apartment building aware of their nightly exhibitions. On day four I took my place by the window with the lights off around 6:30pm. It was the last Friday of the month. Before I could make myself comfortable I saw the door swing wide open. Instead of my two naked nymphs I saw a tall, stern looking middle aged man carrying out a pair of suitcases. While he went out the apartment two young men who were probably his sons came and retrieved several of the the girls’ heavier belongings. As the young men left, my nymphs came out the door each holding light items. They were moving out. Based on the friendly banter among all of them it was clear that their evening exhibitionism was not a factor in their moving out. I felt heartbroken. I wanted to believe that their evening shows were for me and me only and it was only a matter of time before some form of communication took place between us. Instead they gave a good three day show and now they were gone. I wanted to find some kind of reason or excuse to go up to them and talk. ‘Do you guys need some help?’ Then I imagined their tall, stern faced father/uncle glaring at me with a murderous look and shaking his head. ‘We’re good. Thanks.’ I turned on the lights and peered at them boldly from my window. I wanted them to at least see me. The younger one was passing out the apartment and spotted me. She gave me a long curious stare while she walked and came across her sister/cousin and she began whispering in her ear and they both stopped and looked at me and then giggled. Feeling like a creep I drew back the curtains and came out of view. What now? Maybe they would stop by and say their goodbyes? Maybe I was just being pathetic? I lay in bed trying to ignore my conflicting feelings. In the shared kitchen I suddenly heard voices. Some of the boys in my apartment were hanging out or ‘liming’ as we call it here in Trinidad. They were talking about the girls who left and apparently one of them finally confided about seeing them naked at nights and they all started sharing stories of the girls’ daily naked ritual. Funny how they all never said a word to one another prior to this shared witnessing. They started some scuttlebutt on the identity of the girls and stories they heard about them from friends. Most of what they spoke of sounded like bullshit. I wanted to join in the conversation but it just seemed miserable. One of them was drunk and with a really high-pitched and whining voice and another spoke in such depravity that it was clear that given the chance he might’ve raped both girls. Outside I could hear a scuttling noise. The rat was making his rounds looking for fresh garbage. The rat was a much more industrious and respectable fellow than all of us humans who allowed the sight of two naked girls to turn us into primal beasts. I decided to call it a night.

What actor or actress got cast in a role that they normally wouldn't play and absolutely crushed it? Everyone I know who saw Along Came Polly (2004) agrees that the standout comedic performance was… not Ben Stiller (The Ben Stiller Show, There's Something About Mary, Meet The Parents etc) nor Jennifer Aniston (Friends, Office Space, Bruce Almighty) nor Hank Azaria (The Simpsons, Futurama, Mystery Men) nor Debra Messing (Will and Grace, Ned and Stacey) The person who outperformed these four seasoned and well known comedians with decades of experience in film and television (and they were all excellent) was this guy. Phillip Seymour Hoffman At that point in his career Hoffman did not have the level of acclaim as he does now. He was mostly known for his eccentric supporting roles in mostly dramatic films such as Boogie Nights, The Talented Mr. Ripley, Happiness and The Big Lebowski. Just a year after starring in this zany comedy he played the role of Truman Capote in the the film Capote (2005), won the Oscar for Best Actor and from then on his status soared with him being called the greatest actor of his generation. It helped that his role was that of washed up actor Sandy Lyle who believes himself to be of the highest pedigree (despite never having a single role since a hit comedy in the 80s). Hoffman nails it with his character’s sometimes pompous, sometimes laidback mannerisms. He makes it seem effortless in that unique, low-key Phillip Seymour Hoffman style of his It's a pity that he died in 2014, at the prime of his professional career. He was finally being truly recognized for his talent and given leading roles. In my honest opinion, his performance in Doubt (2008) is without a doubt his greatest performance. I'm of the view he even outstaged Meryl Streep in their scenes together. I would've loved to see him take on more comedic roles. I think that he put his heart and soul into his performances and added his own subtle nuances to his characters. Even if you are like critics and don't think much of Along Came Polly, it's hard to hate Hoffman's unforgettable performance as Sandy Lyle.

What Scorsese film would have been better if directed by Spielberg and vice versa? Interesting question. In regards to Spielberg doing a Scorsese film, I know I may be in a minority but I never had much love for Scorsese's Gangs of New York (2002). I've never been able to sit through the entire film. In my honest opinion, just because the epoch the film is based on is an ugly period in history, it doesn’t mean that the film has to be inherently ugly. In the comparable and far superior Once Upon A Time in America (1984), Sergio Leone captures the pockets of childhood innocence and warm camaraderie in a truly poetic manner despite the inherent ugliness of the period documented. In Gangs of New York everywhere looked like a filthy trash heap. All the main characters were assholes. Everyone was somehow dressed in the most rattiest rags they could find. I think Scorsese was a little heavy handed in demonstrating the chaotic grittiness of the period. With the exception of Daniel Day Lewis the entire cast gave mediocre performances. The colours and camera work of the cinematography was glaring and unsettling and the whole revenge arc story didnt seem to have much of a point in the context it was used. In a nutshell the film was just a pointless, ugly film that just happened to have a measure of historical accuracy. Spielberg is the King of demonstrating the humanity that can be found in the absolute darkest periods of history. He does this without undermining historical accuracy or succumbing to fluffy melodrama. Of course the chief examples being Schindler's List and Saving Private Ryan. I think if Spielberg was given the job to direct Gangs of New York, the final product would've been a superior film with fleshed out, relatable characters, a better plot and overall a much more engaging experience for the senses. In regards to Scorsese doing a Spielberg film, I think the there is one film that was right up Scorsese’s alley that I think Spielberg’s did a disservice. Scorsese's eye for realism and portraying characters in their raw, unlikable form would've created a better product. No. It's not Munich (2005) It's Catch Me if You Can. The film was a the feelgood blockbuster movie of 2002. Frank Abagnale Jr was the antihero everyone couldn’t help but love, especially when portrayed by hearthtrob Leonardo DiCaprio. I enjoyed the movie when it premiered but it has aged poorly as of recently. Abagnale Jr was not just a scammer, it has been revealed that he is also a pathological liar. Much of the events described in his book are either grossly exaggerated or completely untrue. When you watch the film now you are treated to a self-indulgent, ego-stroking feast of fakery. I think Scorsese would've been a bit more skeptical towards the author's story and do the proper research into Abagnale Jr's life. The story would've been less attractive and a lot more cynical with moments of downright nastiness (very much in the vein of Raging Bull and The Wolf of Wall Street) but it might have been a compelling portrait of a fractured individual who thought more of himself than he actually was. It definitely wouldn't have the embarrassment that Catch Me if You Can suffers from today. So in conclusion, Spielberg and Scorsese should’ve simply traded director seats in the year 2002.

How did your boss respond when you told him/her you quit? I worked evenings doing pizza delivery some years ago. I performed well and had a good reputation by my coworkers and customers. However I suffered when it came time to head home after work. The taxi situation was dire and I would be stranded in the streets desperately trying to hitch a ride home. 'Can I use my delivery scooter to go home with?’ I begged the delivery manager over the phone an evening. 'It's very difficult for me to get home at nights.’ 'Sorry,' he replied, 'Company policy….’ The company apparently had great fears that I would steal their beaten up, little scooter that bore a fat, moustachioed Italian on the surface of its storage box. And this is after 5 years of service to them. I even offered to buy the scooter on a payment plan but he still refused. I then asked for a transfer to a branch closer to home. He agreed to that idea and seemed to have actually been making some phone calls to get the transfer done when suddenly he called to give me some bad news. 'The position has been taken.’ 'What?’ I said, 'By who?’ 'Ms. Nelson's (a restaurant manager) daughter applied to work delivery. She wanted a location close to home. They gave her the location you wanted.’ He seemed genuinely sorry for me and explained to me that he was delivery manager and not human resource, thus he had no power in regards to staff allocation. It hit like a ton of bricks. Five years I had dedicated to the company and all I asked for was a transfer close to home and they gave it to some girl fresh out of high school who kinda wanted to try deliveries and had connections. The delivery manager begged that I stay stating that most likely the girl wouldn't last and then I could get the position. He was right. The girl didn't last, but still the position was given to someone else. When I got the news again, I immediately sent in my resignation. However my delivery manager was in the process of retiring. After I resigned I heard that the new manager allowed all delivery riders to go home with their scooters/motorcycles if they wanted. It was like three consecutive slaps in the face.

Have you ever lost any respect for someone instantly? I once had a supervisor who I had absolutely no respect for. No matter how much my more coolheaded coworkers advised me to just let him ramble on and just nod my head in silence I couldn't help but say what was on my mind to him. You see, his approach to the supervisory role was sleazy at best. He basically implied to us all that he was our boss. According to him: 'There's my work and there's your work.’ ‘His work' entailed: Funny enough when I heard that he would be appointed my supervisor I was happy to hear the news. Only a few years ago I hung out with him as he was a friend of my brother. We knocked back a few beers and discussed the organisation and the amount of favoritism, bloated and unnecessary hierarchy and the gross amount of people who get paid for doing practically nothing. He mentioned then that if he ever rose in the ranks he'd change that. Six years later he's comfortably become exactly what he preached against. I got into so many vicious arguments with him that it led to physical threats on both sides that in the end I was transferred to another branch. Unfortunately for him he suffered from severe psoriasis which worsened as time progresses. I remember seeing him at the head office, a year after our meltdown and my transfer and he looked at me as though wanting to say something. I couldn't bring myself to talk to him. A month later I heard he was in the intensive care unit at the hospital in regards to a heart condition. A week later I heard that he died. I felt awful that I didn't reach out to him that moment. Made me wonder if I was aware that there was a strong chance I would be dead soon, would I act in the careless manner in which he did at work. I forgive him of course but I can't deny the fact, at the time, he had lost every ounce of respect I had for him.

What are some examples of style without substance in writers? I know I may be critized for some of my choices but these are some of the works I've read that I deeply consider to be style heavy but severely lacking in substance imho. Fight Club — Chuck Palahniuk The cult status of this novel has become almost legendary after the film debut in 1999. Back then I thoroughly enjoyed the film for its defiantly anarchist undertones and its twist ending. As I've grown older the film now seems a tad ridiculous and childish and the so-called twist ending makes absolutely no sense in retrospect. Our of curiosity I read the book and it further confirmed my sentiments that the book/movie was written solely for an audience of angst-ridden males between the ages of 16 — 25. Palahniuk's style is some sort of mish-mash stream of consciousness dialogue combined with frenetic pacing, little concern for character development, cliffhangers around every corner and throws in a random fact few pages (gasoline and orange juice can be used to make napalm……oooh {angst filled teen wets himself}. The Beach — Alex Garland Another 90s, stream of consciousness, style heavy writer who's found enormous success with the titular novel which found its way to the big screen back in 2000. Like Fight Club this novel was aimed at disenchanted 16 — 25 year olds tired of the rat race, capitalism etc. More meaningless pretentious philosophizing, even less character development, throw in a dash of romance, a pinch of melodrama, a teaspoon of surrealism and you have a style heavy book that (just like Fight Club) leans on a great idea rather than on good writing. The Short-Timers — Gustav Hasford Another style heavy novel that coulda been. This Vietnam war account is the basis for the famous film Full Metal Jacket (1987) by Stanley Kubrick. Kudos to Kubrick who did away with Hasford's overbearing stoner prose and stuck to the meat of the novel which was the clever boot camp dialogue and harrowing recruit training. The book is semi autobiographical. It seems as though the moment Hasford is free to roam the streets of Vietnam his writing became almost unreadable in a drug induced haze of (again) stream of consciousness babble. Black Spring — Henry Miller One may be surprised to find an established writer like the controversial Henry Miller on this list but after turning the obscene into an art form with Tropic of Cancer he wrote Black Spring which becomes rather unreadable and unintelligible after the first few pages. Miller's gift is to seize your attention within the first few lines in his writing. He shocks you with his unwholesome combination of literary mastery combined with smut and depravity. He explodes within the first few pages with prose so electric that even George Orwell dedicated an essay in praise of him. However his flaw is his inability to sustain this style at length as he goes from captivating to dull and rambling. Black Spring is a perfect example of that flaw. And last but not least The Trial — Franz Kafka Yes. One of the world's greatest writers is also guilty of style over substance, most noticeably in the above stated novel. If there is one author who has cemented a style for himself it has to be Kafka as kafkaesque is now an accepted English word for anything related to paranoia and fantastic surrealism inspired through stifling bureaucracy. The Trial is not a bad book imho. In fact it is the most representative of his style. However one cannot help but lean towards believing whether the work is a testament to his genius or the whimsical ramblings of lonely, neurotic mild-mannered man. I tend to lean towards the latter as halfway through the novel it seems as though his unique style can't help but disguise the fact that there is no real story of substance happening. But these are all my honest opinions. Love em or hate em.

Is it superficial that I lost interest in a guy because he proudly said that he hasn't read any book in his life? Here's the point of view of a somewhat bookish male. First of all I would say that you've started wrong by considering something he claims about himself. A man (a many women in general) will say all kinds of things to give some kind of impression. In his case he is bragging that he doesn't like books/reading. He probably comes from a rugged environment where reading books is looked down upon as dandyish, antisocial and/or overly sensitive. I come from such an environment. Trinidad is a literate country but for males the stereotypical clumsy, scatterbrained geek who hides behind books because he is afraid to tackle worldly experiences is a prominent stigma. Even if you speak meticulously with proper English words that contain more than two syllables you are regarded with suspicion. Many females are raised to avoid these type of men. Him being proud not reading books is, to me, an ego driven declaration of machismo. You shouldn't let that be a deciding factor though. When younger I always sought after intellectual type girls with whom I could discuss the arts, philosophy, politics, classic literature etc. Sadly relationships never seemed too work out with for a myriad of reasons the chief problem being a severe lack of emotional intelligence. Now that I'm older, the last quality I look for in a woman in how much books she has read in life. Literacy and intelligence are two completely different types of wisdom and I would argue that the latter is far more important than the former. Just because he doesn't read doesn't mean he is any less wise, thoughtful, caring and responsible than the average guy. I've met too many literate women who are a financial and emotional trainwreck to allow for the notion that book reading is a make or break factor in a relationship. Just my two cents.

What is your most interesting encounter with the police? I was working pizza delivery some years ago. I had a delivery to make at what is called ‘the old airport.’ It is a collection of buildings located at what used to be the official airport of the country some decades ago but has long since been discontinued since a more modern airport has been built nearby. As such the ‘old airport’ is now used to house a few airport related businesses and airport administration. It is rather a quiet, relatively vacant area in comparison to the actual airport and no one pays it any mind except for the people who wait for the bus there. One afternoon I dropped off a pizza to a lady who worked at the local Swissport that was located there. While riding the motorcycle out I was stopped by a police vehicle. The driver beckoned me to come over. The glass of his vehicle went down revealing a middle aged male officer behind the wheel and an attractive young female officer at the passenger’s side. The male pointed to some arrows on the surface of the road. Apparently I had entered along the exit arrow and was leaving along the entrance arrow. It was a really petty issue. Nobody cared about those arrows since the old airport was no longer in use and hardly any vehicle ever came there to begin with. Regardless I apologized to the officer and explained to him that I never noticed those arrows until now. Expecting him to let me off the hook and return to my duty I stood in silence waiting. ‘License and insurance,’ he then says in a stoic tone. ‘Is this guy for real?’ I thought to myself. I went to my wallet for my license and while searching I heard the guy explain haughtily to his female sidekick how he busted a pizza delivery man who didn’t even have a driver’s license but was working delivery and how he believes that regular check ups like this reduces the amount of accidents that occur on the road. From the tone of his voice I could sense that the man was trying to make some kind of impression on his female partner and that she was on some kind of training with him. Looking at her face I could sense that she was quite fed up the partner she had been assigned to for the day but was trying to be patient with him. I showed the officer my license. ‘And the insurance?’ Never in my years of working delivery had an officer ever asked me for insurance. The restaurant I worked for was a major chain and police generally knew that this franchise did not make joke with their insurances. Regardless I showed him the insurance title taped inside the back of the delivery box. ‘What’s this? What’s this?’ the officer bellows. ‘All insurances must be presentable for officers to inspect.’ The officer demands that I yank it off from the back and hand it to him. Another petty call. I pulled it off from the box and handed it to him. Meanwhile he barely looks at it but begins to chastise me about how dirty my bike looked and that I should be more prideful of my duty when delivering people’s food and how people die from food poisoning every day. He saw that I had another order to deliver. I was expecting him to send me on my way. This had gone on long enough. ‘What’s in that bag there?’ ‘It’s another order.’ ‘I know!’ he bellowed, ‘What is it?’ Did this man really want me to call out the order that someone made for a pizza? I explained to him it was a pepperoni and pine pizza. ‘Are you sure?’ ‘Yes,’ I replied and I was about to show him the customer’s bill when he said, ‘Take it out the bag and open the box.’ At that point his partner had had enough and she cried loudly, ‘Curtis are you some kind of ass?’ She folded her arms in defiance and shook her head. There was a silence and Curtis the officer proceeded to awkwardly laugh off the situation. ‘Pizza man,’ the officer said in a tone that showed a measure of humility, ‘Pay attention to the road. Don’t let us have this conversation again.’ With that said Curtis the officer returned to his vehicle. His female sidekick gave me an apologetic look with eyes that seemed to say ‘Believe me, you don’t want to be in my shoes right now’ and with that they were gone. I drove off myself, wondering where exactly Curtis was going when he asked me to open the pizza box. Did he expect me to have a stash of cocaine hidden there? Did he want me to try and bribe him by offering the pizza? God alone knows.

Why would I kill a mugger in self-defense? Are my valuables worth more than their life? I’ve been mugged four times. Two of these muggings were violent. In these muggings I had my face punched relentlessly. I had a beer bottle smashed on my head, requiring stitches. I had a gun pointed at my face. I got my pants and underwear torn open and had to walk to the police station afterwards with my junk in my hands. In both muggings I got laughed at by the muggers. I’ll never forget the moment when one of the muggers looked at me sitting defeated on the curb, robbed, bleeding and beaten. I’ll never forget how in the silence that followed he looked me in the eyes and growled ‘That’s how it is.’ In that situation I’m certain that same mugger would’ve killed me if needed. I felt a deep cynical hatred in him; that beating me to a pulp satisfied some inner rage he compartmentalized towards society. No. It wasn’t just about the money for them. They felt the world owed them something that they themselves couldn’t fathom what. What is it that I had that was so valuable to these muggers? In total I lost around $300 TT (43US), a cheap cell phone and wallet with my identification cards which would’ve been no value to them. Someone who so callously and casually engages in theft while inflicting violence upon his victims is someone who has agreed that they do not value your life nor theirs. Why must I pay special consideration to their lives while being beaten senselessly or having a knife or gun pointed at me? Does the small amount of money lost bother me? No. What bothers me is the reality that there are some people out there who saw me like garbage and inflicted a hateful beating while threatening my life, knowing fully well that the loot probably wasn’t worth it. My valuables may not be worth more than a human life but if in self defense I had fatally shot my armed and/or violent mugger, I would not be sending flowers to his family nor showing up at his funeral, nor would I suffer any sleepless nights over it. As the old folks in Trinidad love to say; how you make your bed is how you lie on it.

What "poverty food" is actually really delicious? Trinidad has many types of delicious poverty meals that stem from colonialism, slavery and East Indian indentureship. Some are despondently looked upon with embarassment while others are now expensive delicacies that tourists pay, 'ah pound and ah crown’ for. Poor poverty meals These are the meals that really represent someone going through hard times. These are the delicacies prepared from the remnants of the pantry and hunger induced experimentation. Rice and butter As the name suggests, boiled rice grains soaked in butter. Actually it's not butter but margarine, as real butter here is more expensive than most meats. Exceedingly unhealthy but much more delicious than you would imagine. Just imagine the taste of mashed potatoes except it's rice. Flour porridge Heat some white flour on a skillet and just before it's about to burn throw in some condensed milk and water. This is a Haitian recipe but used by many older Trinis who want to feel full but can't afford to buy groceries. According to how well you garnish this concoction, it can be a hidden delight. Plain egg rice When you have one egg and a bag of rice and you need to feed an entire family, this is the meal of choice. Basically you heat up some boiled rice and throw in a well beaten egg. You will be astonished at how far one egg can stretch. Green fig (banana) with ‘butter’ and salt A family with a couple of banana trees in the yard could be saved from starvation with this simple, delicious meal. Boil a couple full but unripe bananas (with or without skin) and serve with margarine and salt. A fully developed green fig well soaked in margarine with a dash of salt can beat meals in most 5 star restaurants. Banana fritters Instead of throwing away your near rotted bananas, mash them to a pulp, knead in some flour and deep fry in oil. Even when eaten cold these fritters are a treat. Rich Poverty Meals These were meals made from ingredients the upper class and colonial masters would discard such as chickens’ neck and pig's tail. Now they are culinary delights that tourists flock towards and are quite expensive to make/purchase. Chicken Foot souse Don't run away just yet. This flavor will knock your socks off. This is basically boiled chicken's feet soaked in a zesty broth. You'd be surprised the amount of meat a chicken's foot can give. Geera neck Dont throw away those chicken necks! Season them with cumin roast them on a skillet for a spicy snack. These are popular 'cutters’ or bar foods, made to sober up drunkards. This can be made with chicken gizzards also. Fried chicken livers My mother would carry us to this seedy looking bakery on a Sunday where they served fried chicken livers, mostly to satisfy the patrons of the bar that was situated next to them. You'll spit out its overly pungent flavor at first try but it gets tastier after each bite. Pig tail Pig tail meals are now synonymous with special events such as birthday parties and wedding receptions. Pig tail pelau, as shown above, is made from rice and pig tails cooked in caramelized sugar (stewed) with peas and whatever garnishes desired. There is also pig tail soup. A pig's tail is incredibly meaty, tender and juicy that so much that many people find themselves sucking at the bone upon finishing. Black pudding Thanks to our English rulers of yesteryear who brought this excrement looking sausage, made entirely of pig's blood, to the Caribbean. Our version includes a lot more spices and this dish is quite popular served in bread as a street food. It looks and sounds horrid but it is quite creamy textured and rich in taste. and lastly Cow heel soup Who would've known that a cow's heel would be so gelatinous, meaty and soak up flavour so well. Along with fish broth and corn soup, this is the definitive soup of Trinidad.

What's the best "tourist trap" you've ever fallen into? Personally I've never fallen into this scheme but whenever I visit our tiny sister island of Tobago I roll my eyes seeing the amount of tourists who get caught in this trap. Imagine this… You’re on vacation with your family in the Caribbean island of Tobago, known for its stunning blue beaches and laid-back, bohemian lifestyle. As many tourists do, seeing that it's the closest beach to the airport, they spend their first day on Store Bay, the most commercially popular beach in Tobago. As you arrive down the steps, past all the numerous souvenirs, handicraft and food stalls, you look for a nice shady area on the sand to lay your beach towel and make camp. Unfortunately all the good spots are taken so you whip out that suntan lotion and decide to take in some Vitamin D because you'll be taking a dip in the water anyhow. Suddenly a sinewy barechested young man looking like this: Comes with a beach umbrella, and while taking puffs of his marijuana spliff, he stabs the umbrella into the sand amongst you, which provides much appreciated shade from the enhanced Vitamin D plus sunrays that are making you sweat. You think, 'Wow, what nice thoughtful people these Tobagonians are.’ You thank him but he doesn't seem to hear you. He leaves and you assume that the umbrella is complimentary of whatever tourism board is running the country as you notice practically everyone has an umbrella like yours. The man returns with a couple of beach chairs. You jump up ready to assist this helpful man. His mind seems distant as he stares towards the sea horizon as though expecting something. You say thanks again but he leaves without a word. You enjoy yourself in the sun and sea, taking a few splashes in the azure waters. Discussing plans for the evening with your spouse, watching the kids frolic on the sand. An old boat adorned in bright colours arrive on shore blasting music from its speakers. You see a bunch of people get up and head towards the boat. It's apparently a glass bottomed boat that tours the nearby beaches. The man magically appears behind you. ‘Yuh wah go on de glass bottom boat?’ he says. You take some time to translate his sentence and you quickly say yeah. He whips out a card of tickets and a pencil and writes a note under some tickets. He then leads you and your family to the boat and assists you all in helping climb onto it. What great hospitality! What great people! What a nice country! They really do go above and beyond for the tourists. These are the thoughts you think whilst enjoying the tour, staring at the beautiful sights while the children look at fishes and coral through the glass bottom. The tour lasts about two hours and when you return you decide that you will stay on the beach for the sunset. When the sun sets most people are leaving and you see your man along with others like him collecting their vacated beach chairs and umbrellas. You watch the sunset and fall in love with the country. Your man is somewhere behind you smoking another spliff and enjoying the sunset with you. However he seems to be scowling. You tell yourself that maybe that's just his countenance. Never judge a book by its cover. You decide to wrap things up and as you and your family assist in dusting off the beach chairs and folding and the umbrella, your man comes over with a few shirtless friends and takes over that duty. He is staring at you and you don't know what to say. 'Thank you for everything,' you say awkwardly, 'You've been so kind…..What's your name?’ 'Yuh have $1200 (TT) dollars for us sir.’ he says in a gruff, solemn tone while staring you in the eyes. His friends are poised nearby smirking at the scene. 'You didn't tell me you were charging me all this time! You didn't tell me the cost?’ You look at him and his men who look agitated and upset and you look nervously at the near deserted beach. You know that quarreling over money with a bunch of unknown, sinewy shirtless locals would not be a good idea given the circumstances. 'Brudda, if yuh don't mind’ said one of his friends, 'We real busy. Y’all went overtime. Jus pay we for our services nuh.’ He is saying this more as a growling threat than a request. You do your calculations. $200 US should cover the fee and give you back a little more than $100 TT change. You grudgingly give him the money. He looks at it, pockets it and he and his men leave without a word, laughing at something they were discussing, not even considering your change. You've just been schemed my good friend. Lesson #1 in coming to Tobago as a tourist. Absolutely nothing is free. Edit: Did not expect this little gem of advice to take off so quickly. But please be aware that these sort of schemes and unwholesome attitudes are mostly prevalent at Store Bay. The rest of Tobago is very easy going and trustworthy. The Government is doing its best to curb these type of characters from tainting our image. This is just a lesson to be on the alert if you do decide to visit our marvelous country. Edit 9.01.22: Those guys who try to scheme you with their beach chairs and boat rides in Tobago are nothing compared to the ‘trailer trash' of Trinidad. Click here to read all about it.

Have you ever come back to your vehicle only to find something quite unexpected? I worked pizza delivery some years ago at a branch that was located in a rather iffy town. I used to park my vehicle at the tiny parking lot in the back. There was a dumpster that was located in the parking lot that attracted a lot of drug addicted homeless men who would scour the garbage for some odds and ends of food. One night we worked late and I stayed back after the store closed to give a ride to three ladies who would've been stranded waiting for taxis that late hour. I waited as they swept, mopped and balanced the cash register. An hour later they are finally done and we head to the back to the parking lot. Something looked odd about my pickup and upon closer inspection I saw that one of the glass windows at the door had been smashed with several tiny fragments of glass scattered in the back seat and floor. There was a gaping hole near the dashboard where my deck had once been located. The culprit had smashed a $600 glass window to get in and steal a beaten up, old car deck that probably had a $100 value at best. Having your car deck stolen is pretty commonplace around the world. However what was really unexpected was the reaction of the ladies with me. One of them chastised me for being such a fool for not parking my vehicle to the front of the store. The other found the ordeal somewhat amusing and told me that I should be happy that they didn't hotwire and steal the pickup. The third simply walked off and took a taxi without any comment. These were older women whom I had consistently remained after work to offer a ride being concerned for their safety. None of them even pretended to show any sympathy for what had happened to me. While I swept out the broken glass off the seats and floor, the remaining two stood there trading insider work-gossip and never made an attempt to assist me. I wanted nothing more than get in my vehicle and leave them there but I told myself that I would be the bigger person and go through with what I promised. I drove them homewards in silence. After that experience I stopped offering rides to stranded co-workers unless they were good friends. I used to feel so sorry for many of these ladies working fast food but I later realized that many of them are there not because of circumstances but because of their own ignorance and selfish attitudes. It took me a broken window and stolen deck to learn that lesson.

What screams "I'm pretending to be upper class"? My cousin David lived for two years in Trinidad after his upper-middle class parents decided to return to their homeland to retire. David did his SATs at ISPS (International School of Port of Spain), a school which caters to mostly foreign upper-middle/upper class students. It was there that he befriended Carlos. Carlos was a Venezuelan who had an immense stroke of luck. Carlos came from a very poor family in Venezuela and was said to be adopted on a charitable impulse by a rich Texas oil man. Carlos’ foster father didn't intend to have much of a relationship with him but rather wanted to make a point of turning Carlos' life around. He shipped Carlos off to Trinidad and ISPS and left with him a sizable monthly allowance to finish his SATs and pursue a college degree. It was there that Carlos met my cousin David. David did not like Carlos in the least bit. Carlos was the biggest show-off/braggart at ISPS. His first action upon being set to his own devices was to rent a furnished luxury apartment in Goodwood Park (the Beverly Hills of Trinidad). With this apartment he gained fame for hosting weekly parties for his fellow schoolmates laden with weed and alcohol. Like most of Carlos' ‘friends’ David befriended Carlos solely for the opportunity to be invited to these parties. Carlos' attendance at school and his grades soured but he didn't care. He took out a Range Rover and after a drunken night racing along the North Coast he crashed the vehicle and had it wrote off. It was a miracle that he survived and ought to have been an epiphany to change his ways. He didn't. His two years in ISPS were spent indulging, fraternising, boasting, drinking, smoking, chasing girls and maintaining the image of being the most popular student at ISPS. He wasn't the most popular. He was the most infamous. It was hard to find someone who truly liked him. I would include myself in that category. Once when I was in a restaurant with David, Carlos and a few of David's friends, I realized that I had no money for a meal. I made a joke about it. I told everyone that I would be taxing everyone 5% of their meal for charity as I was broke at the moment. Everyone laughed except Carlos who stared at me in horror as though I cursed God and my mother in one sentence. ‘Don’t go anywhere if you don't have any mah-nee!’ Carlos admonished towards me in a stern Venezuelan accent. It was strange how he was so deeply offended by someone near him making a joke about not having money and begging. Everyone stopped laughing. David paid for my meal making sure Carlos didn't notice. Carlos graduated with failing grades and soon found that his funds were depleted. He would guilt trip several of his ‘friends’ for lodging, reminding them of all that he lavished upon them. He reassured them that his foster father was going to send for him to return to the US. This of course was discovered to be a lie, his foster father had washed his hand of an adult Carlos. He found himself broke and homeless. Carlos still lives in Trinidad. He works an ordinary job and rents an unimpressive furniture-less apartment that is above his means. To this day he still brags about his brief period of wealth. His former colleagues take great pains avoiding him whenever they are aware he is around. Otherwise he would stop them in their tracks to entertain lengthy one-sided discussions about the good old days and would inveigle them to grab some drinks in a fancy pub in which they would listen to his ridiculous plans to score big, be constantly reminded of how much he did for their enjoyment at ISPS and then be forced to pay for the bill that he ran up but can't afford with the promise that ‘Drinks are on me next time amigo.’ Such is the life of Carlos. So to answer the question ‘What screams "I'm pretending to be upper class?”’ People like Carlos.

What movies can you watch all the time and never get tired of watching? Without a doubt Dirty Rotten Scoundrels (1988) is the movie I’d take with me to a desert island. I don't think the movie gets a fraction of the praise it deserves. I think it's the highlight of the careers of both its leads Steve Martin and Michael Caine. I must've seen the movie over 20 times and still it is a delight to sit and watch for its entirety. What makes it endearing as compared to great movies that you only watch once is that it doesn't take itself too seriously. There is no moral or lesson to be learned here. Two dirtbags, one a petty hustler, the other a gentlemanly con artist, make their living by manipulating wealthy, slow witted women. They make a bet as to who would be first to con a simple but good natured soap heiress who just arrived in the village at the French Riviera. What makes this film so rewatchable is that, yes it is silly movie, but it is also a very well written, well executed and thoroughly refined silly movie. The location and cinematography is absolutely gorgeous. The score and soundtrack is a fitting blend of waltzy French classical and sophisti-pop. Mostly filmed on location at scenic locations along the French Riviera, the film is one of the most gorgeous movies I've ever seen. From the beginning Villefranche-Sur-Mer train station to the breathtaking Beaulieu-sur-mer to the lookout at Villa Hier at the end, the film is a feast for the eyes. Not to mention the performances. Both Caine and Martin give stellar performances from a remarkably clever script but Martin steals the show and makes the character Freddy Benson his own in a highly physical role the likes of which only Martin can accomplish. Props also to Glenne Headly who plays mutual target of the leads, demonstrating an innocent charm that wins over the hearts of the conmen and the audience. The film takes a not so pleasant topic and turns it into a rather good natured, comedy film. If it were remade today it would be chocked full of the gratuitous profanity, nudity and sex that is the hallmark of modern day ‘comedy.’ There's not a single F-bomb, nor a sex scene, nor a gratuitous flashing of breasts etc. Frank Oz uses no cheap gimmicks to entertain an audience and as such the film can be enjoyed by the entire family. Watching Dirty Rotten Scoundrels is such a pleasure that watching it feels like a little vacation rather than a movie. I watch it every year as a sort of ritual and I am yet to find another movie that is such a timeless delight.

I got an invitation to a high school reunion where I was bullied. I am successful in my career. I want the satisfaction that I’m doing better than my bullies, but I don’t want to demean myself on that level. Should I go? The fact that you are basing a decision solely on the hurt you felt by underdeveloped humans many years (or decades) ago makes me question the level of your ‘success’ if that is your state of mind. The most successful people I know from high school are the ones who haven't allowed the hurt they've experienced deter them from being decent human beings. They don't let it affect making simple decisions that require just an hour or two of their time, a little small talk here, a little empathy there and would cost less than taking the family to see a movie. This is my class back in '99. If you're trying to spot me I'm the awkward nerd on the far right trying to fit in with the group (I had to invite myself over to the shoot). I had a decent amount of friends but I would honestly say that I didn't really get along with the majority of my classmates. A lot of them were obsessed with MTV lifestyle, being relevant and popular. A lot of them were quite mean to me because I was poor and didn't hide it or attempt to fit into their mould. Also, I had my fair share of encounters with physical and mental bullies. This guy here taking the absolute cake. But I wasn't perfect myself. I could be quite obnoxious, aloof and frivolous and I did act randomly mean to some of my own friends who looked up to me. No child in in the history of high school could be considered a model citizen. High school reunions are not just made up of bullies and assholes. There might also be some of the nice former classmates. Even better, you may meet one or two who were awful back in the day but now matured into caring and sensitive adults. Even better, some of your former bullies might even have the burning desire to apologize to you for all the years of hurt. To go to a high school reunion solely flaunt success to your former bullies reeks of immaturity and borderline narcissism. If the above question is a valid question in your mind then you definitely should not ‘demean yourself’ by going. Just as a final sidenote, I was invited to the above class' high school reunion but chose not to go. Not because of personal dislike but because a special, self appointed committee had formed amongst some the more well-off classmates and they decided to pick and choose who was worthy of being invited to the reunion (my best friends were not invited). No thanks. In a case like that. You definitely ought not to demean yourself by going to such a class reunion.

Have you ever sabotaged food because someone was stealing it? Is it possible to sabotage someone's lunch by accident? Yes it is. I was the saboteur. The idiot saboteur. Summer was a co-worker of mine at a warehouse I was employed in during my early adulthood. She was a nice girl but she would often get entangled in workplace drama with other provocative and emotional females likes herself. Things got so bad with her that her enemies would go to extreme lengths to sully her reputation or cause harm e.g. calling her boyfriend at night using a private number, spread nasty rumors (some turned out to be true) about her amongst her closest workmates. To work in such an environment could make any girl a little paranoid. Summer was no exception. One faithful afternoon I was about to enjoy my lunch in our staff lunch room. Lunch times were staggered at 12–1pm for some 1–2pm for the rest. I would normally take my lunch at 12pm while Summer took hers afterwards at 1pm. I collected my lunch in the staff fridge and heated it in the microwave. I joined my friends in the 'mess hall’ where we proceeded to have a very exciting conversation about what crap to do with our money when we got paid. While tearing into a chicken drumstick someone made a comment that my mother prepared a really nice lunch for me today. I took a good look down at my lunch bowl and my heart sank. This wasn't my lunch! It was the exact same bowl like mine…..with an orange cover, a little better kept though…..but this was someone else's lunch! I tried to keep my cool. I told my friends I needed to reheat my lunch. Scared to death I would chance upon the true owner coming towards the kitchen, spotting me carrying his/her lunch like a bloody beggar-thief I haphazardly threw the lunch back into the fridge and took out mine. I heated it and returned to my friends like a nervous wreck but eliciting no suspicions. An hour later I'm busy at work when a stern voice comes over the loudspeaker. 'Will all members of staff please report to the kitchen area?’ My heart leaped like stallion in heat. This is it. The s**t has hit the fan. My friends ambled towards me all curious-like saying stuff like 'What the hell is this about?’ and 'Hey, you saw Summer come out from the manager's office in tears? What's her problem now?’ I tried to play it cool but did a terrible job. 'Huh? What da f**k's going on? I got an order to finish. This is bulls**t. Summer is a ho.’ It's a wonder none of them suspected me right then and there. For all staff to be called to a meeting at once meant that this was pretty serious. Somebody's gonna get sent home. My hands started trembling. The warehouse director took center stage and with a wary look on her face explained that Summer had just gone to have her lunch when she observed that it was severely tampered with. She explained that the person tampered with the lunch in such an extreme manner as if to send an insulting, threatening message to her. The director asked that whomsoever did such an act to please reveal him/herself. All the while I stood looking like this: While everyone else around me started to giggle quietly. Summer who stood next to the director stared at me and I immediately looked away. No one came forward. The director gave Summer money to buy lunch. Case dismissed. As we headed back to our respective positions my friends made light banter about the situation. 'We have a food molester at the warehouse. Anyone of us could be the dreaded food molester.’ They then began to laugh. That became a running joke in the warehouse. Twenty minutes later Summer comes towards me and I start to quiver like jelly. 'You see anybody with an orange cover bowl when you were at lunch Elijah?’ I shook my head in the negative. 'Sick f**king people we have working here,’ she continued. 'Yeah.' I said flatly, 'Hmmm.’ 'I mean,’ she continued while raising her voice, 'Interfering with my food? If that person has a problem with me I don't care what they say to my face but to know that some nasty sonofab**ch will go so low…….I mean……. it's just sad…….a sad, sick person.’ 'Yeah.' I replied flatly, 'Boy!……..Hmmm.’ She then stared at me like she did during the meeting. 'Elijah. It was you?’ I feigned a laugh and acted as though it was a joke, 'Yeah. It was me. Who cooked that food girl? Taste real good.’ She smiled and shook her head and went her way. I knew that she suspected the culprit to be a female so I was off the hook. Some years later I am employed elsewhere and I encounter Summer on Facebook. After a brief chat I admitted to her that I was the food molesting culprit. She laughed and said she knew. I asked her how did she know. She said that she found out after the meeting that I had a bowl exactly like hers. She had put 1+1 together. I said, 'So that whole time you spoke to me after the meeting. You knew?’ She said yes. She was playing along with me to judge whether I tampered with her food by accident, as she suspected, or if one of her enemies made me do it……..that my dumb reaction to her comments had said it all. ‘……..It tasted really good though,' was all I could think of saying. Lesson learned: When you tamper with a co-worker's food by accident, it's a good idea to go tell them.

Who is an actor who you think looks better older than they did when they were younger? Jordana Brewster When I saw the first Fast and Furious movie in 2002 as a teenager, I always wondered why they cast that passable looking chick as Paul Walker's love interest. To me, she looked like the girl in class who you'd keep in mind as 2nd choice if your crush rejected you. But jokes aside, with the passing of each Furious movie I began to notice that she started to look less and less like a cute girl next door and more into refined and stately woman. The kind of woman a man would be kicking himself for not paying attention to in the past.

My girlfriend is mad at me for "not standing up for her.” She accidentally spilled her drink on a girl in the club. The other girl threw her drink on my girlfriend and her boyfriend shoved me. I grabbed my girlfriend and we left. What should I do? I love pub stories. I have one to share in a similar context. Years ago my friends from work and I would visit a bar that was pretty much a flashy looking dive bar. There was 6 of us. The biggest guy in the pack was Kurt who would always bring his wife (then girlfriend) with him. Curt is some specimen of human. If Dolph Lundgren discovered he had a secret Trinidadian half brother, I would gladly tell Dolph to come check out Curt. Curt is a bug dude. He’s so strong that once, three us at work in the warehouse wanted to play a prank on him. We wanted to restrain him on his forklift and bound him onto it with shrink wrap; keeping him there until somebody discovered him. The three of us combined could not subdue Curt and our prank failed. Curt has a great sense of humour when it comes to pranks but when it came to his wife's safety, all jokes ended there. So six us were in this bar taking turns shooting pool. Kurt and his wife were sitting on bar stools against the wall while the rest of us were around a pool table. Suddenly a sound of a beer bottle crashing onto the floor could be heard from the opposite pool table. A pudgy little manchild held his pool stick as though ready to fight someone. His drunken girlfriend released a cackling laugh and was making a poor attempt to subdue him. Apparently the pudgy guy was drunk and believed some guys outside the bar were throwing sweet words towards his woman. He broke his beer as a show of machismo towards the men outside and proceeded to hurl threats their direction Curt and his wife were laughing at something else at the moment. Pudgy guy’s eyes narrowed in on them believing them to be mocking him. He took his girlfriend's beer and hurtles it into the air where it lands and splashes beer upon them both when it smashes near their feet on the ground. Everything went silent. My friends and I at the pool table believed that this was going to be a brawl like no other. Pudgy guy had already provoked the men outside who seemed ready to thrash him and now Curt Lundgren was ready to give Pudgy a demonstration. However Curt is a smart individual. He recognized immediately what was going on and calculated the outcome. Three agitated men ready to fight outside the pub, one drunken idiot stirring up more trouble every second that passed and his girlfriend seeing the whole thing as a joke, broken glass everywhere. If Curt engaged in a fight things would get ugly and his wife could get seriously damaged. Instead Curt decides that we should leave. Without a word we headed to our vehicles and went home. Had Curt been alone he would given Pudgy what he deserved. However bar fights do not play off like they do in those 80s action movies. Everyone involved gets hurts and some even get scarred, maimed or killed. The bar has since closed down after the owner got killed in a drive by shooting last year.

What advice changed your life financially? Observing people’s lives rather than listening to their advice is what inspired my spending habits. So many people who draw some sort of salary have advice about spending that money. Spending advice is at every corner I turn. Here are some examples of such advice I encountered : I get that sort of advice practically everywhere, whether it be my co-workers, acquaintances and within my family, everybody is willing to guide me on how to save a couple bucks here and there with their helpful hints. But one thing that I can never discuss with them is this one taboo question, 'Are you satisfied with the direction of your life?’ Such a question would be considered condescending so such conversation is avoided. I look at the person giving me advice and ask myself does he/she lead the kind of life I want. Do I really want to be that guy stuck in a unfulfilling job to ensure that I pay off my car loan, coming home to an apartment to eat a can of Goya beans every evening? I've met so many people who base their lives around simple analogies: ‘You’re only young once.’ ‘Life is short.’ ‘You can’t eat money.’ ‘Treat yourself.’ ‘Work hard, play hard.’ Regardless of their responsibilities and obligations in life these are their core beliefs and they believe they have the wisdom to offer advice to all listening ears based on their beloved ambiguous three word quotes. In my view this is just a convenient mindset in which one can deny accountability for one self. ‘Honey I'm sorry but I can't pay rent this month. I was hanging out with the boys and one thing leads to another. Life is short. Can you borrow some more money from your parents?’ ‘No I'm not selling my car. This is a limited edition. I'll pay you back what I borrowed before the year is over. Life is short and you can't eat money.’ Sad to say these are the same kind if individuals who are most vocal when it comes to giving advice, personal and financial. If someone's personal lifestyle does not agree with you then do not follow their financial advice. One always goes with the other. In a nutshell I would advise that you stop listening to financial advice from those who place more value on emotional satisfaction. Just my 2¢. A donkey can bray as loud and as often as it feels to but it can never convince anyone that it is a horse.

What has an employee said that immediately caused you to fire them? Jerome (not real name) was a new worker with a big mouth. He was 28 years old at the time, quite older than most of the guys he worked with like myself yet he acted, at best, like a spoilt 15 year old. He was always talking. He always had an opinion about something. He always had to question even the most simple orders and instructions. He believed himself to be the most intelligent person to ever walk the floor of the warehouse and always spoke at length of all the flaws he saw in our system and what he would do to fix the business if he were in charge. Our job was simple: a retail store wants products that we have, we go out with our grocery carts, pallet jacks, forklifts etc, get the products and have them packaged and ready for delivery in the morning. Not Jerome. Jerome's job was to distact you from what you were doing to talk shit about the company and how the money wasn't worth it. He would quote some nonexisting OSHA law that the company wasn't complying with and how he could sue the company if he wanted to. He would discuss his harebrained, get rich quick schemes that he never had to guts to actually attempt. He bragged about his family in the US waiting for him and how he didn't need to work himself like a slave for chump change like we did. At any given day he probably put out 20% of the output of the average worker. He was on a six month probationary period of which it would be decided whether he would be contracted as a permanent worker, given extended probation or let go. No one expected him to be permanently hired. Everyone basically tried to tolerate him for the six month probationary period as best as they could. However he started taking his shenanigans to the next level. He started making the (typically secluded) shampoos lane in the back warehouse his secret hideout. The lane was quiet, had no cameras and far away from our superiors’ field of vision. He decided to set up a makeshift man-cave behind a pallet of Tresemmé 2 in 1 Shampoo and Conditioner. There he would smoke, talk shit with the rare, harmless worker who came by for shampoos and he would watch rap music videos on his cell phone. At the month's end all warehouse workers were allowed to take from the damaged products. We had our own system of fairness whereby we rotated each worker to get a chance to get first pick among the damages. Jerome couldn't give a rat's ass about the system. During the third month of his employ it was observed that practically all of the best damaged goods had gone missing. A co-worker and myself smelt a rat in Jerome and we went to his man cave while he was on lunch and saw the damages were there hidden in boxes. We reported it to the supervisor who came and saw it. He held an emergency meeting and asked for the person who put those damaged goods in the back to come forward. Everyone eyed Jerome angrily but he remained silent. The supervisor reported the matter to the manager who reported it to the company owner and she immediately put a stop to the free damages giveaway. Now the anger towards Jerome had turned into a bloodlust. However the more angry everyone got the more lazy and defiant Jerome became. He was smart enough to abandon his man-cave after his attempted theft but he still spent more than half his working day loitering and talking shit. Every year the company paid for the company staff to have a party, usually at a classy sports bar or a nightclub. We all looked forward to it including Jerome who discussed at length his intention to get drunk off of free premium drinks and score with one of the pretty head office girls. However, one fateful afternoon the owner of the store had an impromptu meeting with everyone in the warehouse. She explained that the company decided to change the format of the staff party. She explained that it was expensive and inefficient having this party every year when too many employees ran up a bill drinking premium drinks all night and then not being able to come to work the following day. She gave the disappointing news that this time the party would be held at 12pm — 7pm the upcoming Sunday. Jerome released a snorting laugh while she spoke. Everyone in the warehouse went dead silent. No one had ever dared interrupt the owner, far less mock her. 'Excuse me,' she said, 'Is there something amusing?’ 'Nobody ever heard of a party 12 o clock in the afternoon,' Jerome said in his spoilt 15 year old voice. 'I've been to many parties 12 o clock in the afternoon' she replied. 'Yeah, birthday parties for kids' Jerome said smugly and looked about for someone to laugh but found only silence. The owner asked Jerome his name and how long he worked in the warehouse. Afterwards she continued her talk uninterrupted but after the meeting was dismissed she, the manager and Jerome went into an office for a talk. Some minutes later Jerome was seen leaving the compound, he was terminated from the job. Sad thing for Jerome was the owner apparently thought over what he said about the party and changed her mind about it. We were allowed to have our traditional, late into the night, party albeit minus the free premium drinks. We had a great time dancing the night away and toasting Jerome whose big mouth finally done some good for a change. Footnote 6/6/2023: There are a few commenters who seem to doubt the validity of my story on the grounds that 'so how come they didn't just fire Jerome as he's on probation?’ Probation is a process of testing and observing a new worker for short period. We signed a contract that we would be terminated on the grounds of serious offences like drug use, sexual harassment, assault, excessive absenteeism etc. Being a crappy worker and talking shit all day wouldn't get you terminated instantly but would definitely make you fail your probation and would have you under their radar for possible termination, which is exactly what happened in Jerome's case. Please. If you find all of this fantastic and unbelievable you are free to shake your head and scroll down.

What movies do you like but everybody hates, and why? When The Matrix came out, every nerdy boy over 12 sang its praises. Every nerdy boy except me. I liked it (kinda) but I just couldn’t see the big deal about it. The action was good and everyone raved about the whole bullet time camera innovation. The soundtrack was phenomenal and the story and the main characters were intriguing. But I just couldn’t see the big deal. I just thought it was too silly for the movie to try to be deep and philosophical with its sociological commentary and high-brow sci-fi concepts, while at the same time engage in low-brow kung-fu action, psudo-BDSM rave culture, dystopian cyberpunk futurism, all the while having villains that looked like constipated insurance salesmen. I felt like the movie tried to be several things at once and took itself too seriously. I also felt that the movie would’ve been more enjoyable if it accepted how silly its concept was and focus more on its action scenes rather than having practically ever character besides Neo drifting off into some rambling philosophical stoner rant. Whenever I shared these criticisms with my nerd friends, they would turn red as though I demonstrated the most shocking of blasphemies. ‘You don’t get it. The Matrix is too deep for you to understand. Go watch your cartoons.’ That would be their usual response, but years would pass and my assessment would remain the same. THEN CAME THE MATRIX RELOADED I sat and watched it on TV long after its cinema premier. I wasn’t expecting much; some more philosophical sci-fi mumbo jumbo and a few over-rehearsed fight scenes. However, thirty minutes within the film I was finding myself thoroughly entertained. The movie went in the exact direction I wanted the first one to go. From the beginning to end the movie was a feast of God-like explosive superpowers, vast weaponry utilized in slow motion, explosions and swords slicing through speeding vehicles that contain time and space altering kung-fu fighting white rastas who can’t die, even in explosions. The movie relished in its stupidity and made no attempt to continue with the existential brouhaha of the original film. As an acne-riddled 18yo I ate it up like hot chicken soup but practically everyone I knew who worshipped the original, hated Reloaded with a passion. However, as admittedly dumb as it is, I consider it the superior movie. I haven't seen Resurrections yet but seeing that practically everyone loathes it I wouldn't be surprised if it turns out to be the best of the four.

Which TV shows were popular when you were younger that would flop today? Why? Oh man. There are so many shows from the 90s that would flop hard had they been released (as they were) today. These two shows ruled daytime television for a long time in the mid 90s. I think one of the reasons for the success of the two interrelated shows is the fact that they were different and there was nothing else on. These weren't the days of Netflix, streaming, 4K/HD, watch at your own pace, high production value but limited seasons/episodes, hundreds of options to choose from high speed internet TV. These were the days of ‘Damn I missed my show’ cable television, paper TV guides, one new show every few months, low budget production with endless episodes and seasons etc. These were the days of ‘take what you can get’ on TV. HERCULES: THE LEGENDARY JOURNEYS Hercules is this chill, alpha-jock type guy who roams around New Zealand (wearing the same Super V-neck goatskin vest and tight leather pants every day) meeting nice quirky villagers of whom he saves from various villains ranging from petty con-men to full blown freakish monsters. At his side is a short, blond, surfer-dude like Iolaus who is the comic relief character. This is the premise for practically every episode. The show is supposedly set in ancient Greece yet don't be surprised to find English knights, Chinese peasants, Japanese ninjas, Nordic Vikings, Mongolian warlords, Egyptian Pharaohs or any cool and exciting historical anachronism discovered randomly during Hercules’ wanderings. The always well-shaved Kevin Sorbo would never break a sweat or mess up his lovely long hair in fights. Everything always worked out well in the end for Hercules, Iolaus and the villagers and if things got truly icky then you know it would take a second or third episode for the villain to be destroyed or for Iolaus/a love interest/a child to recover from near death. XENA: WARRIOR PRINCESS It’s pretty much the same thing except the leads are women. Xena (previously a minor Hercules villain on the show) atones for her past by going around saving helpless villagers with the aid of her short, blond quirky bard Gabrielle and the village idiot Joxer. Unlike Hercules, Xena had more personality and a rather interesting ‘Ay ya ya ya ya’ war cry accompanied with more of a focus on action scenes rather than Hercules’ constant spew of Dad jokes. The show became far more popular than its predecessor and ran from 1995 - 2001 whereas Hercules began in 1995 as well and ended 1999. Comparing these two shows with the crop of fantasy shows that are available now is definitely a chalk and cheese comparison. Take a look at the following screenshots. Now take a look at various people doing Hercules and Xena cosplay: You can barely tell the difference! Historically inaccurate clothing, easily accessible and cheap to film ‘forest’ backgrounds, pampered hairstyles, anachronisms galore, Hercules: The Legendary Journeys and Xena: Warrior Princess were nothing more than glorified cosplay. If either show were released today, as they were, they would be a source for ridicule and memes. However if I can give one positive comment for the show I would have to say that it doesn’t try to secretly force any message down my throat. Xena is a woman who kicks ass. She is not a feminist and definitely not a lesbian as that lame rumour suggests. Hercules doesn’t spout any subtle parables promoting socialism or taxing the wealthy. There is no powerful and evil villain that looks and acts like Trump (or Bob Dole to be more precise with the time). The show is silly and stupid and doesn’t promote any type of political activism. So I’d definitely watch Xena or Hercules over Rings of Power and She-Hulk any time, any day.

The Good, the Bad & the Ugly is an amazing movie but I never understood the scene involving Tuco and his monk brother. As much as it was an emotional scene, it did not advance the movie plot at all. Did Leone ever explain why he added the scene? Yeah. Quite true. But then again, remember, throughout the movie, how often Tuco does this: Everytime he kills or someone is killed through his double crossing, he makes a sign of the Cross. Clearly he has a conflicted relationship with God. It paves the way for the reveal that he comes from a very religious background i.e. the scene with his disapproving monk brother. Admittedly, that scene sticks out like a sore thumb. I guess it was to give an emotional depth to Tuco`s character. It was meant to show that Tuco had a sympathetic, human side to him. Blondie had an emotional side as evident by the short scene where he shared his cigarette with the young, dying soldier. That scene was perfection. However Tuco`s emotional scene didn't play out so well. It tried a tad too hard. Tuco was well characterized and even without this scene one could sense that though he was bad, he wasn't evil. Tuco kept odd standards of decency, unlike Angel Eyes who was a psychopath. Before the monk scene, the movie had established a macho aesthetic of manly indifference. These guys were looking for gold, not for emotional closure. Then this overwrought scene comes in and goes on too long and is a bit unlike Tuco`s persona. He was too hardened from years of crime and debauchery to care about the opinion of his monk brother who he considered a fool or even his recently deceased father who he obviously didn't have a good relationship with. If I were Leone I would write the scene as Tuco`s brother (who is not a monk) informing him that he is headed towards their father`s funeral and grudgingly invites Tuco to pay his final respect. Tuco, feeling a bit remorseful and embarrassed considers the offer but reflects upon the possibility of Blondie escaping and the lost chance of getting gold, makes an excuse and declines. It would be less than 2 minutes long. But it isn’t too off putting and that is why to this day it's still my favorite movie of all time.

What should I absolutely not do when visiting your country? TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO Avoid hiring 'local tour guides.’ Stick to official touring groups from your hotel or large hiking groups. You’ve come to Trinidad on a vacation but you don't want to be so 'touristy.’ You don't want to sign up for the generic cross country tour the hotel is offering. You don't want to be crammed in a bus with a bunch of khaki short wearing, middle aged couples who want to stop the bus every 10 minutes saying. 'Hey driver, look there's a natural spring there. I want to fill my water bottle.’ Or 'Ooh driver stop the bus. I want to get a picture of those local Trinidadian cows.’ And you definitely don't want to go on the same well beaten hiking track where ten buses like yours are parked so more tourists like yourself could commence on a 5 minute hike, past dozens of souvenir stalls, to see a dormant mud volcano which, if you're lucky, might belch out a nauseating scent of rotten eggs. It sounds awful but believe me the other option is far worse. You'd meet someone who'd tell you, 'I know a guy who does private tours. He'll take you to the real hidden sites that the tour groups don't go and he's very knowledgeable of history and professional. You don't have to stick with the dull tourist tours.’ You want to make the extra effort and discover the hidden Trinidad (or Tobago) and this guy sounds like the real deal. Here are the problems with that offer: Discovering a makeshift stone axe . My Scottish cousins realized this too late when they hired some guy who was a friend of a friend of friend who did private tours. He was taking them to Turure Water Steps which was indeed a beautiful place with four amazing waterfalls, each bigger than the last. When I heard he was charging $1000 TT (roughly 150 US) to take them there I protested and told them that they were being ripped off. Anyone could take them there for free. They argued that he was a professional and had deep knowledge of the history of places. I went along with them for the trip. Some hours later, returning home, they agreed that they were ripped off. In summary the lesson learned here is that there are several people like that so-called tour guide who wants to rip off hapless tourists. Either you stick with your hotel tour or if you want to go off the beaten track, join a professional hiking/tour group or go with a large group of friendly, trustworthy locals. Doing otherwise could have you ripped off or even worse. Edit 31.08.21 Had no idea this little tidbit of info would've garnered so many upvotes. Thank you all for the support.
